newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Upside bias seen into OEX expiry.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Upside bias seen into OEX expiry.

text.p: The expiration of April S&P 100 index could give the underlying market an upside bias into the close.
April OEX options officially expire Saturday after finishing trading on Friday.
By about 1430 CDT/1930 GMT, the OEX was up 1.66 at 743.87 after having rallied to 746.79 intraday.

Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said the OEX expiration is shaping up to be similar to the expiration of April S&P 500 index options, which went off the boards Friday morning.
"The same thing is occurring now that occurred last night on the SPX," he said, explaining that the just in-the-money calls were trading at a premium to their intrinsic value.
The OEX April 740 calls were trading at 4-3/4, up one point in late trade Friday.
"Last night, SPX 760's were bid 2-5/8," Schwartz explained. "The index was 761.76. It was a premium of almost a point with a big open interest."
Open interest in the OEX April 740 call was 19,462.
Schwartz said the cash settlement value for the SPX was 764.70, 4.70 better than the 760 strike.
"They came out far better," he said, referring to the investors who held the SPX 760 calls rather than selling them late Thursday.

"My conclusion is that when the open interest is high and they're trading at a premium right down to the wire, the bias has to be on the buyside because the crowd must be intending to exercise and benefit from the higher close rather than selling here for cash," he said.
The OEX April 740 calls had traded 16,460 contracts by late session. The busiest action was in the April 740 puts, which traded nearly 30,000 contracts.
The April 745 call traded about 29,000 and the April 745 put traded roughly 27,300.
Traders said Thursday that speculators were buying up some of the April OEX calls, betting that the market's rally would outpace the time decay and easing in implied volatilities.
April marked the second month in a row in which speculators were buying the expiring options right up to the end, traders said.
